title: A 20-Second Rickshaw Reel From Kolkata's Pujo Has Redefined 'Winning at Life' Online
excerpt: CESC employee Abhishek Mukherjee, his wife and their son, singing along on a hand-pulled rickshaw ride between pandals — a clip shared by an educationist and praised by Sanjiv Goenka has viewers rethinking success.
body:
• A 20-second selfie video of Kolkata couple Abhishek Mukherjee, his wife and their young son riding a hand-pulled rickshaw while pandal-hopping during Durga Puja has gone viral on X.
  • Educationist Amit Kilhor shared the clip on Thursday as an example of what winning at life looks like, calling it 'Exemplar A' for defining success.
  • RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group chairman Sanjiv Goenka identified Mukherjee as a CESC Ltd employee and praised the family for capturing the joy of Pujo so naturally.
  • The family itself has not commented: the Times of India said it tried to reach Mukherjee through CESC officials but could not connect with him as of late Thursday.

It lasts 20 seconds. A middle-aged couple and their young son smile into a phone camera from a hand-pulled rickshaw, singing along as festival lights dazzle behind them on a Kolkata street during Durga Puja. There is no spectacle in it — and that, viewers have decided this week, is exactly the point.

How a family clip became a definition of success

The video began circulating widely after educationist Amit Kilhor shared it on X on Thursday, presenting it as an example of what winning at life actually looks like. Kilhor called the clip 'Exemplar A' for defining success. The framing stuck: the Times of India reports that the reel prompted conversations about happiness, family, and the habit of equating success with material wealth. One account, peek_humour, joked that Elon Musk is still only the second richest man in the world — the richest, by the clip's arithmetic, being the man in the rickshaw.

"Some moments have a way of bringing a smile to everyone's face."

— Sanjiv Goenka, Chairman, RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group

The employer's chairman joins in

The story gained a second life when Sanjiv Goenka, chairman of the RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group, shared his praise. Goenka identified the man in the video as Abhishek Mukherjee, an employee of CESC Ltd, the group's flagship power utility, and said it was heartening to see a member of the CESC family capturing the joy of Pujo so naturally and winning hearts. Mukherjee's wife and son are not named in the coverage, and the family has not spoken publicly: the Times of India said it contacted senior CESC officials to reach him but could not connect with him till late on Thursday.

Not everyone wants it analysed

The comment threads split in predictable directions. Some viewers read the clip through gender roles — one user, Ritika, took it as an illustration of Bengali men sharing household responsibilities and appreciating their wives, sparking a debate on that reading. Others pushed back against reading anything into it at all. A user posting as Mishhteeee cautioned against treating the rickshaw ride as a sign of poverty, noting that Durga Puja traffic restrictions make a rickshaw a practical way to move through Kolkata's festival streets, and urged people to stop overanalysing a moment of family joy.

Amid a festival famous for elaborate pandals and spectacular illumination, the clip's appeal is its scale: one family, one rickshaw, one short ride between pandals. For the diaspora watching Pujo from other time zones, that may be the most recognisable image of the festival there is.
